en.metaDescription: Live online Tajweed classes for learners who can already read the Qur’an. Study articulation, Noon and Meem rules, Madd and stopping through guided recitation.
en.title: Online Tajweed Classes for Clearer, More Accurate Recitation
en.intro: Learn the rules of Tajweed step by step and put each one into practice as you recite. Your teacher listens, explains what to adjust and helps you build recitation that is accurate, steady and consistent.
en.imageAlt: Illustration of a student reciting from a Mushaf on a stand, with articulation points, letter characteristics and Madd marked as topics

features.title: For readers
features.text: Suited to learners who can already read Quranic text, even if slowly.

features.title: Live recitation

audience: Learners who can read the Qur’an and want to recite it with correct Tajweed.
Children and teenagers ready to move from reading to applying recitation rules.
Adults who learned to read in the past and want their recitation reviewed and corrected.
learn: Where each letter is articulated and which characteristics shape its sound.
The rules of Noon Sakinah and Tanween: Izhar, Idgham, Iqlab and Ikhfa.
Meem Sakinah rules and where Ghunnah is held.
The main types of Madd and how long to extend them.
When letters are pronounced heavy or light.
How to stop and resume recitation at suitable places.
en.outcomesIntro: As you progress, the course works towards helping you:
outcomes: Recognise common Tajweed rules when you see them in a verse.
Apply the rules you have studied while reciting, not only in theory.
Notice and correct your own frequent pronunciation mistakes.
Recite with a steadier rhythm and more consistent elongation.
Understand which areas of your recitation still need focused practice.
en.requirements: You should be able to read Arabic letters with their vowel marks, even if slowly. If letters and vowels are still new to you, Tarteel Qaidah or Quran Reading is a better starting point. You will also need a device with a camera, stable internet and a quiet space; a Mushaf or digital copy you can follow is helpful.
en.lessons: Each lesson pairs a short explanation of a rule with recitation of verses where it appears. You recite, your teacher points out what to adjust, and you repeat until the correction feels natural. Rules from earlier lessons are revisited during recitation, so they are applied together rather than in isolation.
en.planNote: Your teacher reviews your recitation during the free trial and adapts the order and pace of these modules. Progress depends on attendance and practice; no completion date is guaranteed.

guide.title: Tajweed, Quran Reading or Quran & Tajweed?
guide.text: All three programs involve reading the Qur’an aloud. The difference is where they start and what they concentrate on. You can talk through your current level during the free trial before settling on a program.

items.title: Quran Reading
items.text: Concentrates on learning to read Quranic text and building fluency, from letters and vowel marks to words and verses.

items.title: Tajweed
items.text: For learners who already read and want to study the rules of recitation and apply them accurately.

items.title: Quran & Tajweed
items.text: A combined path that builds reading foundations and introduces essential Tajweed within one learning plan.

journey.title: Book a free trial
journey.text: Choose Tajweed in the booking form and tell us what you would like to improve.

journey.title: Recitation review
journey.text: Your teacher listens to you recite and notes which sounds and rules need attention.

journey.title: Rule-by-rule practice
journey.text: Study each rule with examples, then apply it while reciting verses.

journey.title: Guided revision
journey.text: Revisit earlier rules in longer passages and discuss what to focus on next.

faq: Do I need to read the Qur’an fluently before starting?

You need to be able to read Arabic letters with vowel marks, but you do not need to be fast. If letters and vowels are still new to you, Tarteel Qaidah or Quran Reading may be a better first step; you can discuss this during your trial.
How is this different from the Quran & Tajweed program?

This program concentrates on Tajweed rules for learners who already read. Quran & Tajweed combines reading foundations with essential Tajweed in one plan, which can suit learners who still need reading support.
Is the course only theory?
No. Each rule is explained briefly and then practised in recitation, with your teacher correcting you as you read.
Can children study Tajweed?
Yes. Explanations, examples and the amount of terminology are adapted to the learner’s age and reading level.
Are lessons live?
Yes. Lessons are live online with a teacher, one-to-one or in a small group depending on your needs, so your recitation can be heard and corrected during the lesson.
Can I ask for a female teacher?
Musliman Academy has female Quran teachers for sisters and young girls. Mention your preference in the message field when you book your trial.
How long does it take to learn Tajweed?
It depends on your starting level, how often you attend and how much you practise between lessons. Your teacher can suggest a realistic pace after hearing your recitation.
How do I start?
Book a free trial, choose Tajweed as your program and tell us about your goals and preferred class time.

en.intro: Start from the Arabic letters and their sounds, then build step by step to vowel marks, joined words and short Quranic examples. Live lessons with a patient teacher give beginners a solid base for reading the Qur’an.

en.outcomesIntro: The course works towards helping you:
outcomes: Recognise the Arabic letters in their different forms.
Pronounce each letter clearly, including sounds that do not exist in your own language.
Read syllables and words with vowel marks, Sukoon, Tanween and Shaddah.

en.requirements: None. Tarteel Qaidah is designed for learners starting from the beginning, so no previous Arabic is needed. A device with a camera, stable internet and a quiet space are enough; a notebook helps for practising letter shapes.
en.lessons: Your teacher introduces a few letters or a single reading rule, models the sound and asks you to repeat and read examples. Mistakes are corrected as they happen, and each lesson revisits earlier material so new skills rest on firm ground. Short practice between lessons helps the sounds become familiar.
en.planNote: Your teacher checks what you already know during the free trial and starts from the right point. Pace depends on attendance and practice; no completion date is guaranteed.

guide.title: Where Tarteel Qaidah fits
guide.text: Tarteel Qaidah is the starting point for reading. It teaches you to decode Quranic text accurately; it is not an Arabic conversation course and does not teach the meaning of words.

faq: Is this suitable if I don’t know any Arabic letters?
Yes. The course starts with the letters and their sounds, so no previous knowledge is needed.
What is the difference between Tarteel Qaidah and Quran Reading?

Tarteel Qaidah builds the foundations: letters, vowel marks and basic reading rules. Quran Reading continues from there with reading words and verses and developing fluency. Your teacher can help you decide during the trial.
Will I learn to speak Arabic?
No. This is a reading course focused on reading Quranic text accurately. For vocabulary, grammar and communication, explore our Arabic Language program.
Can young children join?
Yes. Lessons are adapted to the learner’s age, attention span and current level. Share the child’s age when you book so the trial can be planned accordingly.
How much practice is needed between lessons?
Short, regular practice is more useful than long, occasional sessions. Your teacher will suggest what to review before the next lesson.
Are lessons live?
Yes. Lessons are live online with a teacher, one-to-one or in a small group depending on the learner’s needs.
How long does the course take?
It depends on the starting point, attendance and practice between lessons. Your teacher can discuss a suitable pace after the trial.
How do I start?
Book a free trial, choose Tarteel Qaidah as the program and tell us about the learner’s age and preferred class time.

faq: How is this different from Islamic Studies?
Islamic Values for Children concentrates on character, manners and everyday behaviour. Islamic Studies covers broader foundational knowledge such as beliefs, worship, Seerah and Islamic history.
What age is this program for?
The program is designed for children. Lessons are adapted to each child’s age and understanding rather than fixed age groups, so please share your child’s age when you book.
Does my child need previous Islamic knowledge?
No. Lessons start from your child’s current understanding.
How are values taught?
Through short stories, questions, discussion and familiar examples, so children can see how a value applies to their own choices.
Are lessons live?
Yes. Lessons are live online with a teacher, one-to-one or in a small group depending on your child’s needs.
Can I follow my child’s progress?
Yes. Parents receive follow-up and progress updates, and you can share any values or habits you would like the teacher to focus on.
How long does the program last?
There is no fixed length. Values are revisited over time, and the pace depends on attendance and your child’s needs.
How do I start?
Book a free trial, choose Islamic Values for Children as the program and tell us your child’s age and preferred class time.

faq: Who can apply?
Quran, Arabic and Islamic Studies teachers, Ijazah holders, students of knowledge and others who want to teach non-Arabic speakers more effectively.
Do I need teaching experience?
The form includes an option for applicants with no experience as well as for experienced teachers. The team uses your answers to suggest a suitable training path.
Is the training only for Quran teachers?
No. It is designed for Quran, Arabic and Islamic Studies teachers working with non-Arabic-speaking learners.
Is the training online?
Yes. Training takes place online, and you can choose a preferred training time in the form.
What happens after I submit the form?
Our team reviews your request and contacts you to discuss your background, goals and the suitable training path.
How long is the training?
Duration and schedule depend on the training path agreed with you. The team will share the details when they contact you.
Will I receive a certificate or Ijazah?
This is a teaching-skills program, not an Ijazah program. Please ask the team about certificate details when they contact you so you receive current, accurate information.
Does the training lead to a teaching position?

The training focuses on developing your teaching skills and does not guarantee employment. If you are interested in teaching with Musliman Academy, choose that as your training goal in the form and the team can discuss it with you.
